paragraphs: Yochanan, brother of R' Dosa ben Horkinas.

In Yevamot 16a: When R' Yehoshua, R' Elazar ben Azariah and R' Akiva came to R' Dosa ben Harkinas regarding the matter of a daughter’s co-wife, in whose days a daughter’s co-wife was permitted to the brothers [for levirate marriage], in accordance with Beit Shammai, and the Sages thought this was the view of R' Dosa ben Harkinas, but he told them that he had a younger brother, and he is a firstborn of Satan (and the gaon abbreviated צה״ח remarks that it should read, 'a sharp young man'), and Yonatan is his name, and he is among the disciples of Shammai: 'Take care lest he overwhelm you in halakhic debate, since he has with him three hundred arguments that a daughter’s co-wife is permitted.' In Hyman’s account, he met R' Akiva, challenged and stumped him, [and] said to him: 'You are that Akiva whose name goes from one end of the world to the other; happy are you that you merited a name, yet you have not yet reached the cattle herders.' And in the Yerushalmi there, chapter 1, halakhah 6, it is related somewhat differently that Yonatan, brother of Rabbi Dosa, was explaining to them why a daughter’s co-wife is permitted, and due to his great sharpness they did not understand his words.
